questions.question: What is the purpose of the Booth Algorithm in multiplication?
options: To perform binary addition using only shift operations
To reduce the number of partial products in binary multiplication
To convert decimal numbers to binary representation
To implement division using repeated subtraction
questions.explanation: The Booth Algorithm reduces the number of partial products by examining pairs of bits in the multiplier, thereby decreasing the number of operations required for multiplication.

questions.question: In the Booth Algorithm, what action is taken when the decision bit pair is 01?
options: Arithmetic shift right (ASR) is performed
Add the multiplicand to the accumulator
Subtract the multiplicand from the accumulator
No operation is performed
questions.explanation: When the decision bit pair is 01, no addition or subtraction is performed; instead, an arithmetic shift right (ASR) is applied to the current value.

questions.question: What happens when the decision bit pair is 11 in the Booth Algorithm?
options: The accumulator is incremented by the multiplicand
The accumulator is decremented by the multiplicand
An arithmetic shift right (ASR) is performed
No addition or subtraction is performed
questions.explanation: When the decision bit pair is 11, no addition or subtraction is performed; only an arithmetic shift right (ASR) is applied.

questions.question: In the Booth Algorithm, what is the role of the Q-1 bit?
options: It acts as a carry bit for addition operations
It is used to determine the next operation based on the current and previous bits of the multiplier
It stores the final result of the multiplication
It is used to initialize the accumulator to zero
questions.explanation: The Q-1 bit, along with the current Q bit, forms a decision bit pair that determines whether an addition, subtraction, or shift operation is performed.

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct step in the Booth Algorithm when the decision bit pair is 10?
options: Add the multiplicand to the accumulator
Subtract the multiplicand from the accumulator
Perform an arithmetic shift right (ASR)
No operation is performed
questions.explanation: When the decision bit pair is 10, the multiplicand is subtracted from the accumulator, which is equivalent to adding the two's complement of the multiplicand.
